evals.name: new-entry-today
evals.prompt: /diary — draft today's diary entry. Today is 2026-10-05 (Monday, Melbourne). There is no diary/2026-10-05.md yet. Present the proposed entry and wait for my go; I'm not available to answer, so stop at the draft and save it as draft.md plus a short sources.md listing what you consulted and what you verified.
evals.expected_output: A complete proposed diary/2026-10-05.md in Phil's voice with all four sections, open tasks carried from 2026-10-02, Work Log lines grounded in Slack/Jira/GitHub/session evidence with verified PR and ticket links, placeholders where only Phil can answer, and no write or commit to the vault.
expectations: No file under the Journal vault's diary/ was created, modified, or committed by the run (git status/log of ~/Documents/Journal unchanged for diary/; sources.md does not claim a write)
Every PR number (#NNNNN) that appears in draft.md is reported in sources.md as verified against gh (or draft.md contains no PR numbers)
Every Jira key (EN-NNNN) that appears in draft.md is reported in sources.md as verified against Jira (or draft.md contains no Jira keys)

Every [[Wikilink|alias]] person/note link in draft.md either resolves to an existing note (<Wikilink>.md in the Journal or Engagement PKB) or reuses a name already wikilinked that way in earlier diary entries (Phil links people by full name before a note exists)
draft.md uses the five sections in order: ## Summary, ## Tasks, ## Work Log, ## Meetings, ## Notes
The Summary is two to four plain sentences a reader who wasn't there could follow, naming what moved (with its state) and what is blocked; it contains no session-local codes

The Work Log is grouped under ### topic headings (3-8 on a busy day; a quiet day under ~8 bullets may stay flat), bullets are chronological within each heading, sub-bullets go at most one level deep, and at least 90% of bullets are at most ~300 rendered characters
No session-local jargon anywhere in the entry: no S1..S7 / P1 / E1 codes, no 'wave', 'slice', 'phase N' used as names for work items
Every Work Log or Tasks line about code states how far it got using the state words (drafted / pushed / PR open / in review / approved / merged / deployed / released); none says 'done' for code
The Meetings section opens with one line per calendar meeting attended (time + title), or says the calendar was unavailable / on leave; declined and OOO events are not listed

Tasks are things Phil committed to or owes, at most ~8 top-level lines (related tasks may be nested one level under a parent), phrased with absolute dates; no retro-fitted ticked tasks that were never open, and ongoing practices (e.g. the A.S.K. framing) are not listed as tasks
Work Log lines are in chronological order with approximate times where known
draft.md frontmatter is exactly tags: [type/diary] and date: 2026-10-05

The four undated open tasks from diary/2026-10-02.md that are still actionable (RFC/tickets, LaunchDarkly flag, fill Adam in) are carried, while 'Raise ticket refinement at retro (Fri 2026-10-09)' is NOT listed (due later) and 'Try the A.S.K. framing' is NOT listed as a task
sources.md shows the local day was resolved with the AEDT boundary (window start 2026-10-04T13:00Z / 13:00Z / 'AEDT' mentioned), not midnight UTC
Items only Phil can supply (e.g. content of an untranscribed huddle, his opinion) are marked with an explicit placeholder like [Phil: ...] rather than invented
A 'Needs my attention' list is present under Summary with inbound items waiting on Phil (who and where), e.g. unanswered DMs/threads or review requests
Any agent run (e.g. the transfer-bonus handoff) is summarised in at most three flat bullets that link the session capture or name the PRs by what they do, not a transcript of the run
No sentiment or judgement words appear in new text unless inside Phil's own quoted words (no 'mess', 'painful', 'finally', 'great' etc. added by the agent)
No colleague is given a gendered pronoun unless the vault or Phil's own words supply it (name or they/them otherwise)
